solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bedlam at university — paddle round river

indicators.note: round here just places the paddle beside the river, finishing the word around it

parts.note: being up means in residence at a university
an oar is a paddle for rowing

explanation.surface: A student describes chaos at college, rowing round the river.
explanation.walkthrough: UP is the British idiom for being in residence at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam and an uproar are both scenes of noisy chaos, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Severely criticise the German seen in Bow

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it severely
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A harsh critic attacks a German performer seen in Bow, in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow looks like a London district, but it is the verb meaning to defer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pander is to defer or give in to someone's wishes, a figurative bowing down.

clue.text: Gold box Rubbra emptied for ensemble

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a chest is a large box

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside of the composer's name, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A gold box belonging to the composer Edmund Rubbra is cleared out for a musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: Rubbra was a twentieth-century English composer, apt for the musical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large musical ensemble of instrumental players.

clue.text: Car stuck on shore no good

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: a ship that runs aground is stuck on the shore

explanation.surface: A car stranded on a beach is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' tells you to remove G from RUN AGROUND. In British usage a runaround is a small car kept for short local journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaround is British slang for a small, cheap car used for local errands.

clue.text: Lids seen to flutter in dalliance?

indicators.note: eyelids that flutter move about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Fluttering eyelids are a sign of flirtation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks dalliance as only one kind of idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance in the sense of idle dawdling or wasting time is a form of idleness.

clue.text: One cold room over in chilly regions

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word for room is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: room in the sense of space to move

explanation.surface: A single cold room is all there is in frozen lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SPACE into ECAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar ice caps are the permanently frozen, chilly regions at the poles.

clue.text: Six-footer to be left Bible among reformed drinkers

indicators.note: among puts the Bible version within the drinkers' letters

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, an organisation of reformed drinkers
the RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A tall person leaves a Bible with a recovering alcoholics' group.
explanation.walkthrough: Six-footer suggests a tall person but means an insect, which has six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the immature stage of an insect, an animal with six legs.

clue.text: North American food wife leaves as snack

indicators.note: leaves means the wife's letter goes out of the word for food

parts.note: chow is slang for food

explanation.surface: An American wife walks out leaving food as a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' drops W from CHOW to give CHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip topped with cheese, eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Rehearsed play possibly flat on stage?

definitions.meaning: in sport a ... is a practised move from a dead ball
a flat is a painted scenery panel

explanation.walkthrough: Flat is the theatre term for a framed canvas scenery panel.
explanation.definitionFit: A set piece is both a pre-planned sporting move and a piece of stage scenery.

clue.text: Settle for section in Beethoven's concerto

indicators.note: section in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A listener settles down for one movement of a Beethoven concerto.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensconce oneself is to settle comfortably in a place.

clue.text: Deliver on location as discussed

indicators.note: discussed means spoken, so the letters are judged by how they are said

parts.note: re means on or about, and a site is a location

explanation.surface: A speaker delivers a talk on site, as previously agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: RE + SITE gives RESITE, which is said the same way as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite a speech or poem is to deliver it aloud from memory.

clue.text: Facing archdeacon, counterpart appears powerless

parts.note: Ven, the Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

indicators.note: powerless means the letter for power is taken away from the counterpart

parts.note: a peer is an equal or counterpart

explanation.surface: An archdeacon's opposite number seems to have lost authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powerless' takes P (power) out of PEER to give EER.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin surface layer, a facing over cheaper material.

clue.text: Moved Laotian area in Asia Minor

indicators.note: moved means the letters of the nationality are shifted into new places

explanation.surface: A Laotian relocates to an area in Asia Minor.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia is the peninsula of modern Turkey, historically called Asia Minor.

clue.text: Outline of waist turning round figure

indicators.note: turning reverses the two edge letters of the waist
the outline of a word is its first and last letters, its edges

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A tailor measures a waistline by turning round a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outline of' keeps W and T from waist; 'turning' reverses them to TW.
explanation.definitionFit: Two is a number, and a figure here means a numeral.

clue.text: Society stops consortiums reformulating failed policy

indicators.note: stops means the letter for society plugs a gap in the reworked letters
reformulating means these letters are made up afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A society blocks business consortiums from rewriting a policy that has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformulating' turns CONSORTIUMS into TRUSONOMICS; S goes inside. Trussonomics was Liz Truss's short-lived 2022 economic plan as UK Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The tax-cutting economic programme of Prime Minister Liz Truss collapsed within weeks in 2022.

clue.text: Broken rule again produces intermittent pain

indicators.note: broken means the letters of these words are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Breaking a rule again brings on a recurring pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgia is sharp, often intermittent pain along a nerve.

clue.text: Landing light visible in sky?

parts.note: a shooting star seen in the sky that survives to land on earth

explanation.walkthrough: Landing light suggests an aircraft lamp, but it is a light in the sky that actually lands.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor that reaches the ground rather than burning up is called by this name.

clue.text: Old hat banned by doctor penning poem

parts.note: out can mean banned or excluded

indicators.note: penning means holding in, so the doctor encloses the poem

parts.note: MD is a doctor of medicine
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: An old hat was banned by a doctor who was writing a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Banned and penning both read as part of a story about a doctor, but one gives letters and the other is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for something out of fashion or dated.

clue.text: Score with awkward truths in spirited exchange

parts.note: to score is to cut a line in a surface
and means together with

indicators.note: awkward shows the letters of the word truths are arranged clumsily

explanation.surface: Someone scores points by telling awkward truths in a lively argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' turns TRUTHS into THRUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut and thrust, from swordplay, is the idiom for lively, combative argument.

clue.text: Noodle from UK region sort of square

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, a region of the UK
a T-square is a sort of square used in technical drawing

explanation.surface: A kind of noodle dish from a UK region served in a square.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is slang for a silly person, and a nit (nitwit) is a fool.

clue.text: Suspend courier displaying emotional problems

parts.note: to hang something is to suspend it
UPS is the parcel courier United Parcel Service

explanation.surface: Someone suspends a delivery driver who is showing emotional problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Hang-ups are psychological inhibitions or anxieties.

clue.text: Perhaps like Red Baron, flier showed the way

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, a flier
led means guided, showed the way

explanation.surface: The Red Baron, a famous flier, led his squadron.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Baron was the German fighter ace Manfred von Richthofen; flier suggests a pilot but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron holds a rank of nobility, so he is an example of someone with a title.

clue.text: One buried inside in a tomb strangely shows desire

indicators.note: buried inside puts the numeral within the rearranged letters
strangely means the letters of in a tomb are put in an odd new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A person buried inside a tomb oddly reveals a longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns IN A TOMB into AMBTION; 'buried inside' puts I within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambition is a strong desire to achieve something.

clue.text: Stroke — fantastic cut — is making boundary

indicators.note: is forms the boundary, sitting on either side of the other letters
fantastic means the letters of cut are rearranged fancifully

explanation.surface: A cricketer plays a brilliant cut shot that reaches the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges cut; 'making boundary' sets the letters of is on either side. A cut is a cricket stroke and the boundary is the edge of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Ictus is a medical term for a seizure or stroke, and in verse a stressed beat.

clue.text: Trendy? Check out music genre

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
to check out is slang for to die

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a style is trendy and says to check out the music.
explanation.walkthrough: Check out looks like an invitation to listen, but it is slang for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Indie is a genre of rock and pop originally released on independent labels.

clue.text: Alpha male in charge for minute

parts.note: A is alpha in the NATO alphabet
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: The alpha male takes charge for a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: Minute is the adjective meaning tiny, not the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic, as in the size of an atom, is used to mean extremely small.

clue.text: Checked receding water level — dredge in middle

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the word for water level is read backwards

parts.note: the tide is the rising and falling water level of the sea

indicators.note: in middle takes the two central letters of the word dredge

explanation.surface: Receding tide means the water level was low enough to dredge the middle of the channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receding' turns TIDE into EDIT; 'in middle' picks ED from dredge.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to check and correct it.

clue.text: Looking awkward and ugly in an upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of these words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone appears clumsy and unattractive when distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungainly means clumsy or lacking grace in movement or appearance.

clue.text: Hero in poem by American about yard and ship

indicators.note: by means next to, so the American letters follow
about means the poem wraps around the yard and ship

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
SS is the prefix for a steamship
US is short for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: A hero in an American's poem is written about a shipyard.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, for steamship, is the usual crossword ship; 'about' wraps the poem round yard and ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus is the hero of Homer's Odyssey.

clue.text: Plan to have rump in cooking range

indicators.note: in places the rump inside the cooking range

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of cast-iron cooking range
the rump is the end or back part

explanation.surface: A recipe plans to cook a rump of beef in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a heavy cast-iron stove common in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a plan or list of items to be dealt with.
